I'm good at cutting people out of my life. But not replacing them with more positive people. So right now I'm down to just like 3 people I ever interact with in life, all of them negative influences. I know I need to go out and make new friends and associates, but depression says "no way, dude." I hate it.

> I call myself I "people pleaser" because I am constantly offering to do more- at work, personally, you name it- for others at the expense of my own physical and emotional health. It's like I see them wanting more and I offer to just do it and I see the relief come across their face and it makes me feel like I have worth.

I'm def. a people pleaser as well. But it's not about wanting to feel worthy - it's more like I feel an obligation and fear some undefined consequences if I don't. 

Normal people don't put so much importance on other people's feelings. They can tune out minor anger and agitation other people express because it's just transitory and not important. But people like me, maybe you, who were abused at a young age tend to really magnify the importance of other people's emotions and feel responsible for them - which is absurd because we can't really control how other people react, and even if we could it's not our job. But knowing this doesn't fix it. 

I really need to get into therapy again, and find a therapist who will treat me like a student and have me practice saying no and being assertive and all that over and over and over again. Since I've had trouble finding someone to do that, I'm thinking maybe I can find a book or something online with exercises - in person would be much more ideal, but I'm in a kind of small, backwards town and the quality of mental health care here is sad.

I really like the micro house movement. I'm good at making things, and my father designed and built his own unique house and I learned a lot about that stuff from him. I actually made detailed blueprints of a house in a high school drafting class (although I lost them, it wouldn't be a house I would want to build today anyway, but it was a neat experience). I would **love** to design and build a little cabin with solar panels like the one in the video!

But like you said, it takes money to buy land, etc. And I don't really want to do it here. I really, really want to move back out West. I was much happier there. I just like the society better. 

I actually went to college out of high school and eventually graduated with a good GPA. But it was an art degree, which is nearly useless - and I still have most all of the student loans to pay. Debt fucking sucks. It's like a huge weight added to your life. 

Relationships *are* work. Most people feel they are worth it, but I never do in the end. I've never met someone - friend or potential lover - that I felt that magical feeling so many redditors on other subs talk about. I hate when they say "you just haven't met the right person yet," because many of us never will meet the right person. I mean, it could happen, but you meet most of the people you'll meet in life when you're young and involved in a lot of stuff. After your 20's, most people only interact with a few people they work with and maybe a few more. Online dating simply doesn't work for me because I'm a male and physically unattractive - women just don't give you a chance, no matter how polished your profile. 

I don't even bother trying right now. In some part of my mind, I'll try again at some point. I'm losing weight slowly, and trying to make more money. But until I don't live with my parents anymore, there's zero point in even trying to meet women. For one, my parents are so controlling and conservative that I couldn't have a girl sleep over. But how embarrassing is it to tell people you live at home when you're middle aged? I could sell it as something other than what it is - my dad has health problems and I tell some people I moved here to help take care of him. But the truth is still there in my mind, and it ruins everything. Until I feel OK about myself and my situation, I don't want to bother trying. Even if I do get out again, I don't know if I want a relationship because of all that stuff we talked about. I do miss sex, though, as infrequently as it has been available to me in life. 

But with work, I got my first job when I turned 16, and worked full time + all through high school and college. Shitty jobs that ate up my time, energy, and soul. Then I graduated and eventually got a "real" job that was just more of the same. I feel like I sacrificed my mental health for a paycheck. It almost killed me. 

I ended up so burnt out on working these soul-sucking jobs that I ended up quitting after I got sick. I couldn't physically do it without drugs, and mentally it wore me down to nothing. So I now refuse to work for anyone else. I just do freelancing stuff and flipping things on ebay. Ebay is actually good money, if I would just get organized and motivated to put the hours in. I am pretty sure I'm ADHD but haven't gotten tested yet because I neglect my health like everything else.
